lead: Charleston plumbing deals with tidal flooding, hurricanes, salt air and some of the oldest homes in the South. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Charleston.
risk: tidal flooding and backups, old cast-iron and galvanized pipes, and storm damage
why: Homes on the Peninsula and South of Broad date from the 1700s to the early 1900s, with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron drains and old sewer laterals. Many sit on raised foundations with exposed pipes.
King tides and heavy rain flood low streets on the Peninsula and push water up through drains. Hurricanes add surge and long outages.
water: Charleston Water System treats water from the Edisto River and Bushy Park Reservoir. It is soft.
tips: Know king tide dates and your flood zone.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Check historic district rules before exterior work.
Wrap exposed pipes under raised homes before a freeze.
areas: PipeMend works on the Peninsula, South of Broad, Wagener Terrace, West Ashley, James Island, Daniel Island and every other Charleston neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Charleston building inspections office, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation.

faq.q: Why does downtown Charleston flood so often?
faq.a: The Peninsula is low, and high tides back up storm drains. Add heavy rain and streets flood quickly. The city is upgrading drainage, but low homes still need backflow protection.
